guide.title: Principles of Pharmacology & Drug Classes
guide.lead: You don't need to memorise every drug, but you must know what each one you give does, how it gets in, how long it lasts and how it can hurt. Agonists switch receptors on, antagonists block them, and narrow-margin drugs turn dangerous with small changes.

sections.title: Key terms
rows: Binds and activates a receptor (epinephrine on adrenergic receptors)
Binds and blocks (naloxone on opioid receptors)
Activates weakly and blocks full agonists (buprenorphine)
Time for the level to halve; steady state takes about 4–5 half-lives
Gap between effective and toxic dose; narrow for digoxin, lithium, warfarin, phenytoin
The liver breaks down swallowed drugs before they circulate; IV, IO, IM, sublingual, intranasal and inhaled routes avoid it

figures.alt: A receptor drawn as a lock: an agonist key turning it (light on), an antagonist key sitting in it but not turning (light off), and a partial agonist half-turning it.

sections.title: Drug names
items: Generic: the official name – use it (exams and safe practice)
Trade or brand: the maker's name (Narcan, EpiPen)

sections.title: Controlled drug schedules (US)
rows: High abuse potential: morphine, fentanyl, oxycodone, codeine alone
notes: Other countries use their own schedules; the principle – tighter control for higher abuse risk – is the same.

items.label: Complete heart block
items.sub: Narrow-margin drugs (digoxin, beta-blockers) can cause it.

quiz.q: Most important instruction for nitroglycerin tablets:
options: Let it dissolve under the tongue; don't swallow
Hold between cheek and gum and chew
quiz.explanation: Sublingual absorption avoids the first-pass effect.

quiz.q: Older man on warfarin and digoxin with new confusion and nausea. Most relevant drug feature?
options: Both have a narrow therapeutic index
Both are cleared only by the kidneys

quiz.q: Anaphylaxis with stridor and SBP 82: first-line drug and mechanism?
options: Epinephrine IM: alpha (vessels) and beta (heart, bronchi) agonist
quiz.explanation: Treats every part of the reaction.

options: A competitive mu-opioid antagonist that displaces opioids
quiz.explanation: It wears off sooner than many opioids.

quiz.q: Steady state after regular dosing takes about:
Which route is affected by the first-pass effect?
quiz.explanation: The liver acts before the drug circulates.
Bronchodilation; tachycardia is a side effect.
Speeds a vagal bradycardia, dries secretions.

quiz.q: Which name should you use for drugs?
quiz.explanation: Generic names are standard and safer.

flashcards.question: Three drug names
flashcards.answer: Chemical (molecule), generic (official), trade or brand (manufacturer). Use generic names.

flashcards.question: Agonist vs antagonist
flashcards.answer: Agonist binds and activates (epinephrine). Antagonist binds and blocks (naloxone).

flashcards.question: ADME
flashcards.answer: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion: what the body does to a drug.

flashcards.question: First-pass effect
flashcards.answer: Liver breakdown of swallowed drugs before they circulate. Avoided by IV, IO, IM, sublingual, intranasal, inhaled and (partly) rectal routes.

flashcards.question: Narrow therapeutic index
flashcards.answer: Toxic dose close to effective dose: digoxin, lithium, warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline.

flashcards.question: US drug schedules
flashcards.answer: I: heroin. II: morphine, fentanyl, oxycodone, codeine alone. III: ketamine, codeine combinations. IV: benzodiazepines. V: low-dose codeine mixtures.

flashcards.question: Nitroglycerin
flashcards.answer: Ischaemic chest pain: 0.4 mg sublingual every 5 minutes, up to 3. Not if SBP below 90 mmHg, sildenafil or vardenafil within 24 hours, tadalafil within 48 hours; caution in RV infarction.

critical.scenario: Nursing home: 80-year-old on digoxin, warfarin and furosemide, vomiting for 2 days, confused, HR 42 irregular. The nurse asks if she should give tonight's digoxin.
critical.question: Response and management?

options.t: No: suspect digoxin toxicity (dehydration raises levels). Monitor, IV access, fluids per protocol, 12-lead, transport
Give the digoxin: she missed doses

critical.explanation: Narrow-margin drugs plus dehydration and diuretics are a classic combination.
critical.kpi: Recognizes narrow therapeutic index drug toxicity

critical.scenario: Inferior STEMI: after one nitroglycerin his BP falls from 148/92 to 78/50 and he feels faint. Right-sided ECG shows ST elevation in V4R.
critical.question: Cause and next step?

options.t: Right ventricular infarction – preload-dependent; stop nitrates, lie flat, fluid bolus per protocol, pre-alert

critical.explanation: Check V4R in every inferior STEMI before nitrates.
critical.kpi: Recognizes nitrate-induced hypotension in RV infarction

critical.scenario: 24-year-old unresponsive, RR 4, pinpoint pupils; bottles of oxycodone and alprazolam nearby.
critical.question: Pharmacological approach?

options.t: Ventilate first, then naloxone titrated to breathing (not to waking); no flumazenil

options.f: Can cause seizures in chronic users.

options.t: Large naloxone dose to wake him fully

critical.explanation: Benzodiazepines add to breathing depression; support ventilation.
critical.kpi: Applies receptor pharmacology to a mixed overdose
